resources.title: National ID: first application and replacement
resources.summary: How Kenyan citizens aged 18 and over apply for a national identity card, and how to replace a lost or damaged one.

content.eligibility: Kenyan citizens who have turned 18. Replacements are for anyone whose ID has been lost, stolen, damaged or needs correcting.
documents: Birth certificate (original and copy) for first-time applicants
Copies of your parents' ID cards, where available
For a replacement: details of the lost card and, where asked, a police abstract
steps: Visit the National Registration Bureau office in your sub-county or a Huduma Centre that offers ID services.
Fill in the application and have your fingerprints and photograph taken.
Keep the waiting card (acknowledgement slip) you are given — you will need it to collect the ID.
Track progress by calling the Huduma Contact Centre on 1919, then collect the card where you applied.
content.fees: First-time applications are generally free. For replacements, the fee has changed more than once in 2026 because of temporary fee waivers. Confirm the current amount with Huduma Kenya (1919) or on the eCitizen invoice before paying.
content.processing: Not published as a fixed period. Ask at the registration office when you apply.
content.caution: Replacement fees and waivers changed during 2026. We could not confirm the fee that applies today from an official notice.

resources.title: Passport: new applications and renewals
resources.summary: Apply for or renew a Kenyan ePassport online through eCitizen, then attend an immigration centre for biometrics.

content.eligibility: Kenyan citizens. Children apply with a parent or guardian's consent.
documents: National ID (or birth certificate for minors)
Recent passport-size photo as specified on eCitizen
Old passport, if renewing
For a lost passport: police abstract
steps: Sign in to the Directorate of Immigration services on eCitizen and choose a passport application.
Fill in your details, upload the documents requested and pay.
Book an appointment at an immigration centre (for example Nyayo House, Nairobi, or a regional office).
Attend with your original documents for verification, photo and fingerprints.
Collect the passport in person when you are notified it is ready.
content.fees: Published fee schedule: 34-page Ordinary KSh 7,550; 50-page KSh 9,550; 66-page KSh 12,050; replacement of a lost or mutilated passport KSh 20,050. Not every booklet is always available on eCitizen — check the amount shown before you pay.
content.processing: The Directorate's Service Delivery Charter target is 14 working days.

resources.title: Birth certificates (including late registration)
resources.summary: Register a birth and get a birth certificate through Civil Registration Services on eCitizen.

content.eligibility: Parents or guardians of a child born in Kenya; adults whose birth was never registered can apply for late registration.
documents: Birth notification from the hospital or the assistant chief
Parents' ID cards
For late registration: supporting documents such as school or clinic records, as requested
steps: Make sure the birth was notified (hospitals do this; for home births, the assistant chief).
Sign in to eCitizen and open Civil Registration Services.
Choose the application (new certificate, late registration or replacement) and fill in the details.
Pay the fee shown and follow the instructions for collection or download.
content.fees: Statutory fees apply. Huduma Kenya confirmed in 2026 that a proposed fee waiver had not taken effect. The amount for your application is shown on eCitizen before payment.
content.processing: Late registrations take longer because records are verified. No fixed period is published.
content.caution: Third-party guides quote different fees. We only state the fee that eCitizen shows at checkout.

resources.title: Death certificates
resources.summary: How families register a death and obtain a death certificate, which is needed for succession, insurance and pensions.

content.eligibility: A relative or other person responsible for registering the death.
documents: Death notification from the hospital, or from the assistant chief for deaths at home
ID card of the deceased (if available) and of the applicant
Burial permit details, where issued
steps: Ensure the death is notified to the civil registration office (hospitals usually do this).
Apply for the death certificate through Civil Registration Services on eCitizen or at a civil registration office.
Pay the fee shown and collect or download the certificate as instructed.
content.fees: Shown on eCitizen before payment. We could not confirm a current fee from an official schedule.
content.processing: Not published as a fixed period.

resources.title: Marriage registration and certificates
resources.summary: Give notice of an intended civil marriage, get it solemnised and download the marriage certificate on eCitizen.

content.eligibility: Both parties must be at least 18 and legally free to marry.
documents: ID cards or passports of both parties
Photos as requested
Details of two witnesses
Where previously married: proof of divorce or a death certificate
steps: Both parties sign in to eCitizen and complete the notice of intended marriage with the Registrar of Marriages.
Pay the notice fee shown. The notice is published for 21 days so objections can be raised.
The marriage must be solemnised within the period allowed after the notice (reported as 90 days).
Since 13 January 2026 the Registrar's certificates and special licences are generated and downloaded on eCitizen instead of being printed at the office.
content.fees: Shown on eCitizen at each step. Published guides disagree on the amounts, so rely on the invoice.
content.processing: At least 21 days for the notice period.

resources.title: KRA PIN registration
resources.summary: Get a KRA Personal Identification Number online in minutes. It is free and needed for jobs, bank accounts, land and business.

content.eligibility: Kenyan residents with a national ID, and non-residents/foreigners under the separate KRA requirements.
documents: National ID number (or Alien ID for foreign residents)
Active email address and phone number
Employer's PIN if you are employed; business registration details if you run a business
steps: Go to KRA iTax and choose 'New PIN Registration'.
Select 'Individual' and the online form.
Enter your ID details, contact information and tax obligations (or none).
Submit. The PIN certificate is sent to your email and can be downloaded from iTax.
content.processing: Instant once the online form is submitted.

resources.title: Filing your KRA income tax return
resources.summary: Every PIN holder must file an annual return on iTax, even if they had no income (a 'nil return').

content.eligibility: All KRA PIN holders, including people with no income in the year.
documents: KRA PIN and iTax password
P9 form from your employer (if employed)
Records of other income and allowable reliefs
steps: Log in to iTax.
Choose Returns → File Return → Income Tax Resident Individual (or Nil Return).
Enter your income details from your P9 and other records, or file a nil return if you had no income.
Submit and download the e-Return acknowledgement receipt.
content.fees: Filing is free. Late filing penalty: the higher of 5% of the tax due or KSh 2,000.
content.processing: Deadline for individuals: 30 June of the following year. KRA has said the Finance Act 2026 moves the individual deadline to 30 April from 2027.
content.caution: The filing deadline is changing from 2027. Check KRA's notices before the next filing season.

resources.title: Police clearance certificate (certificate of good conduct)
resources.summary: Apply on eCitizen for a DCI police clearance certificate, then have your fingerprints taken at an approved centre.

content.eligibility: Kenyan citizens and residents who need proof of their criminal record status, for example for jobs or travel.
documents: Original ID or passport and a copy
Two passport-size photos
Printed C24 fingerprint form and payment receipt from eCitizen
steps: Sign in to eCitizen and open the Directorate of Criminal Investigations service.
Apply for a police clearance certificate and pay.
Print the C24 form and receipt.
Book and attend fingerprinting at DCI headquarters, a regional DCI office or a Huduma Centre that offers the service.
Download the certificate from your eCitizen account when it is issued.
content.fees: Widely reported as KSh 1,050 including the eCitizen convenience fee. Confirm the amount on eCitizen before paying.
content.processing: Varies by centre. The DCI has piloted faster biometric desks in some towns.

resources.title: Registering a business name or company
resources.summary: Register a business name or a private limited company with the Business Registration Service (BRS) through eCitizen.

content.eligibility: Kenyan citizens and residents aged 18 and over (company directors and shareholders must meet BRS requirements).
documents: ID cards and KRA PINs of the owners, directors and shareholders
Proposed business names (for the name search)
Business address and contact details
steps: Sign in to eCitizen and open Business Registration Service.
Search for and reserve your proposed name.
Fill in the registration form (business name, partnership or private company) and upload documents.
Pay the fee and download the certificate once approved.
content.fees: BRS fee schedule: business name registration KSh 950. Official name search KSh 250. A private limited company is listed at about KSh 10,650 in the BRS fee schedule (its FAQ quotes KSh 10,750) — confirm on the invoice.
content.processing: BRS lists one day for a business name certificate.

resources.title: County business permits
resources.summary: Every business needs a permit from its county government. Each of the 47 counties sets its own process and charges.

content.eligibility: Anyone operating a business premises or trade in a county.
documents: Business registration certificate
KRA PIN
ID of the owner
Details of the premises and type of business
steps: Find your county government's revenue or trade department (online portal or county offices).
Apply for the single or unified business permit for your business category.
Pay the charge set in your county's Finance Act and display the permit at your premises.
Renew it every year before the deadline your county sets.
content.fees: Set by each county's Finance Act and depend on business size and category. We do not list amounts because they differ by county.

resources.title: Huduma Centres and the Huduma Contact Centre
resources.summary: Huduma Centres bring many government services under one roof. You can also get help by phone on 1919.

steps: Check which services your nearest Huduma Centre offers before you travel — services and hours differ between centres.
Carry your original ID and any documents for the service you need.
For questions, call the Huduma Contact Centre on 1919 or email info@hudumakenya.go.ke.
content.processing: Huduma Contact Centre (phone): 7am–9pm Monday to Friday; 8am–6pm weekends and public holidays. Opening hours of physical centres vary — check before visiting.

resources.title: Complaining about a government service
resources.summary: If a public office delayed, refused or mishandled your service, the Commission on Administrative Justice (Office of the Ombudsman) can help — for free.

content.eligibility: Anyone with a complaint about a public office or public officer, including denial of access to government information.
steps: First raise the issue with the office concerned and keep a record (dates, names, reference numbers).
If it is not resolved, complain to the Ombudsman: online, by email, by SMS, by post or in person.
Give your contacts, the office involved, what happened and what you want done.
content.processing: The Commission says it responds within 10 working days of allocating a complaint.
tips: Offices: Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu, Isiolo and Eldoret, plus desks at some Huduma Centres.

resources.title: Land searches and property registration (Ardhisasa)
resources.summary: Before buying land, do an official search to confirm the registered owner and any charges or restrictions.

content.eligibility: Anyone. Searches are done per parcel.
documents: Title number of the parcel
Your ID and KRA PIN (for an Ardhisasa account)
steps: Create an account on Ardhisasa, the Ministry of Lands online platform.
Choose 'Search' and enter the title or parcel number.
Pay the search fee through ArdhiPay.
Download the search certificate showing the registered owner and any encumbrances.
For registries not yet on Ardhisasa, apply at the relevant land registry.
content.fees: Shown on Ardhisasa before payment. Guides quote different amounts, so check the invoice.
content.processing: Online searches are processed after payment; times vary by registry.
content.caution: Ardhisasa does not yet cover every land registry. Always confirm with a lawyer or the registry before paying for land.

resources.title: NSSF: registration and contributions
resources.summary: The National Social Security Fund provides retirement savings. Employers deduct contributions; self-employed people can contribute voluntarily.

content.eligibility: Employees (registered by their employers) and self-employed people.
steps: Employees: your employer registers you and remits contributions every month — check your payslip.
Self-employed: register with NSSF and contribute voluntarily.
Check your contributions and statement through NSSF's official channels.
content.fees: Contribution rates from February 2026 (Year 4 of the NSSF Act): 6% from the employee and 6% from the employer. Tier I on the first KSh 9,000; Tier II on earnings between KSh 9,000 and KSh 108,000. Maximum KSh 6,480 each per month.
content.caution: The rates are from NSSF's notice to employers as widely reported; we could not open the notice itself on nssf.or.ke.

resources.title: Emergency numbers in Kenya
resources.summary: Who to call in an emergency. All numbers below can be dialled free from mobile phones.

steps: Police, fire and general emergencies: 999 or 112 (911 also works).
Medical emergency / ambulance: 922.
Kenya Red Cross: 1199.
Gender-based violence: 1195 (24 hours).
Child abuse or a child in danger: 116 (24 hours).

sources.name: National Ambulance Dispatch Centre launch (Government Advertising Agency)

resources.source_name: National Police Service; Social Health Authority; Kenya Red Cross; Department of Children Services

resources.title: Registering with SHA (Social Health Authority)
resources.summary: Every Kenyan resident should register with SHA, which replaced NHIF. Registration is free.

content.eligibility: All Kenyan residents. Register your household and dependants.
documents: National ID number (birth certificate numbers for children)
Phone number
Details of your dependants
steps: Dial *147# and follow the prompts, or register online at sha.go.ke.
Confirm your details from the national registry and add your dependants.
If you are not salaried, answer the household means-testing questions to set your contribution.
You can also register with help from a Community Health Promoter, at a SHA office or a Huduma Centre.
content.fees: Registration is free. Contributions are reported as 2.75% of assessed household income, with a minimum of KSh 300 a month — confirm your amount on sha.go.ke.

resources.source_name: Ministry of Health — SHA registration guide

resources.title: What SHA covers
resources.summary: SHA pays for care through three funds: primary care, the Social Health Insurance Fund, and a fund for emergency, chronic and critical illness.

steps: Primary Healthcare Fund: basic and preventive care at lower-level facilities such as dispensaries and health centres.
Social Health Insurance Fund (SHIF): the main package for outpatient, inpatient, maternity, surgical and specialist care at contracted facilities.
Emergency, Chronic and Critical Illness Fund: high-cost care such as emergencies, cancer, dialysis and intensive care, including when other benefits are used up.
content.caution: Exact services and tariffs change. Ask the facility whether it is contracted by SHA and what your benefit covers before treatment.

resources.source_name: Social Health Insurance (General) Regulations, 2024 — Ministry of Health

resources.title: Finding public hospitals and health facilities
resources.summary: Use the Ministry of Health's official registries to find any registered facility in all 47 counties.

steps: Search the Kenya National Health Facility Registry (Digital Health Agency) by name, county or code.
The Ministry of Health's Master Health Facility Registry (KMHFR) also lists facilities, but it could not be reached when we checked.
Check the facility level: dispensaries and health centres for basic care; county referral hospitals for specialist care; national referral hospitals for the most complex cases.
In an emergency, call 922 for an ambulance or go to the nearest facility.

resources.source_name: Digital Health Agency — Kenya National Health Facility Registry

resources.title: Checking that a private hospital or clinic is licensed
resources.summary: Before treatment, confirm a private facility is licensed by the Kenya Medical Practitioners and Dentists Council (KMPDC).

steps: Open the KMPDC register of licensed private health facilities.
Search by facility name or county and check that its status is active.
You can also check individual doctors on KMPDC's practitioner registers.
Report unlicensed facilities or misconduct to KMPDC.

resources.source_name: Kenya Medical Practitioners and Dentists Council

resources.title: Maternity care
resources.summary: Antenatal, delivery and postnatal care are available at public facilities and SHA-contracted private facilities.

steps: Start antenatal clinic visits early in pregnancy and keep your Mother and Child Health booklet.
Register with SHA before delivery and confirm the hospital is contracted for maternity services.
Plan how you will get to the facility; in an emergency call 922.
After birth, attend postnatal visits and start your baby's immunisations.
content.caution: Ask your facility exactly what SHA covers for delivery and newborn care before admission.

resources.title: Childhood vaccination (KEPI schedule)
resources.summary: The Kenya Expanded Programme on Immunisation protects children from serious diseases. Vaccines are given at public health facilities.

steps: At birth: BCG and the birth dose of oral polio vaccine.
At 6, 10 and 14 weeks: the pentavalent vaccine, oral polio and pneumococcal vaccines (rotavirus at 6 and 10 weeks).
At 9 and 18 months: measles-rubella vaccine.
Keep the child's vaccination record and ask your clinic about any catch-up doses or campaigns.
content.caution: Schedules are updated from time to time; follow your clinic's advice.

resources.source_name: Ministry of Health — Kenya National Immunization Policy (2023)

resources.title: Mental health support
resources.summary: If you or someone you know is struggling, help is available. In immediate danger, call 999 or 112.

steps: Kenya Red Cross 1199 offers psychosocial support.
Befrienders Kenya offers emotional support for people in distress.
Children and young people can call Childline on 116.
You can also ask for mental health services at a public hospital.
tips: Befrienders Kenya lists its hours as Monday to Friday, 9am–5pm.

resources.source_name: Kenya Red Cross; Befrienders Kenya (via LifeLine International)

resources.title: Donating blood
resources.summary: One donation can help save several lives. Donors are screened on the day to protect both donor and patient.

content.eligibility: People aged 16–65 who weigh at least 50 kg and are in good health. Not during pregnancy or breastfeeding.
steps: Find a blood donation centre or drive run by the Kenya Tissue and Transplant Authority.
Eat and drink well before donating.
Answer the health questionnaire and have a quick finger-prick check.
Men can donate again after 3 months; women after 4 months.
content.caution: The KTTA website (ktta.go.ke) had an expired security certificate when we checked, so we do not link to it.

resources.source_name: Kenya News Agency; Kenya Tissue and Transplant Authority

resources.title: Public health alerts
resources.summary: Official health warnings — such as disease outbreaks — come from the Ministry of Health. Approved alerts also appear in our notices section.

steps: Follow the Ministry of Health's official website and social media for alerts.
Report a suspected outbreak or unusual illness to your nearest health facility.
In a medical emergency, call 922.

resources.title: Floods, drought and disaster preparedness
resources.summary: Know where to get official warnings and what to do before, during and after floods and other disasters.

steps: Watch for weather warnings from the Kenya Meteorological Department.
Follow instructions from the National Disaster Management Unit and county officials.
Never walk or drive through moving flood water; move to higher ground early.
Keep an emergency kit: water, food, torch, phone charger, important documents and medicines.
For rescue and disaster help call 999/112 or the Kenya Red Cross on 1199.

resources.source_name: Kenya Meteorological Department; Kenya Red Cross

resources.title: Booking the SGR Madaraka Express
resources.summary: Book Nairobi–Mombasa SGR train tickets online with Kenya Railways and pay by M-Pesa.

content.eligibility: All passengers. Each passenger needs an ID or passport number when booking.
steps: Open the Kenya Railways eTicketing site (metickets.krc.co.ke).
Choose your route, date, train and class.
Enter passenger details and pay by M-Pesa.
Arrive early — there are security checks at stations — and carry the ID used to book.
content.fees: Reported fares (not confirmed on the KRC booking site at the time of checking): Economy KSh 1,500, First Class KSh 4,500, Premium KSh 12,000 one way, Nairobi–Mombasa. Check the price on the booking site.

resources.title: SGR routes and timetables
resources.summary: The Madaraka Express runs between Nairobi Terminus and Mombasa Terminus, with stops at stations along the line.

steps: Check the current timetable and stopping stations when booking — schedules change during holidays.
Nairobi Terminus is in Syokimau; plan your connection (the commuter train links Nairobi Central and the SGR terminus).
Mombasa Terminus is in Miritini.

resources.title: Nairobi commuter rail
resources.summary: Kenya Railways runs commuter trains from Nairobi Central Station to the suburbs.

steps: Routes include Syokimau, Athi River, Ruiru, Embakasi, Kikuyu and the SGR Nairobi Terminus.
Buy tickets at the station or as directed by Kenya Railways.
Check the latest timetable — services change during works and holidays.
content.fees: Fares on Kenya Railways' commuter FAQ (undated): Syokimau KSh 60, Athi River KSh 80, Ruiru KSh 60, Embakasi KSh 50, Kikuyu KSh 40. Confirm at the station.

resources.title: Matatu routes and fares
resources.summary: Matatu fares are set by operators and change with time of day, demand, weather and fuel prices.

steps: There is no official published fare table for matatus. Ask the conductor before you board.
Use NTSA-licensed matatus belonging to a registered SACCO; the SACCO name is painted on the vehicle.
Report dangerous driving or overcharging to NTSA or the SACCO.
content.caution: Because there is no official source, IMMA News does not publish matatu fare figures. Any fare you see elsewhere is an estimate.

resources.title: Driving licences: new and renewal
resources.summary: Learn to drive at an NTSA-accredited school, pass the NTSA test, then apply for and renew your smart driving licence on eCitizen.

content.eligibility: Applicants who meet NTSA's age requirement for the licence class and pass the driving test.
documents: National ID
Driving school certificate and test results (new licences)
Existing licence details (renewals)
steps: Enrol at an NTSA-accredited driving school and apply for a provisional licence on eCitizen.
Complete training and book the NTSA driving test.
After passing, apply for the smart driving licence on eCitizen and pay.
Renew on eCitizen before expiry by choosing the renewal period.
content.fees: A three-year smart licence renewal is widely reported at KSh 3,050. Confirm the amount on eCitizen.

resources.title: Vehicle ownership transfer
resources.summary: Transfer a vehicle to a new owner on eCitizen. The seller starts the transfer and the buyer accepts it.

content.eligibility: Registered owners selling a vehicle and buyers with active eCitizen accounts.
documents: Original logbook (scanned as PDF)
Buyer's ID number and KRA PIN
steps: Both seller and buyer activate their eCitizen accounts.
Seller: open NTSA → Motor vehicle services → Vehicle transfer, upload the logbook and enter the new owner's details.
Pay the fee shown.
Buyer: sign in and accept the transfer.
The new owner confirms the vehicle under 'My Vehicles'.
content.fees: Shown on eCitizen for your vehicle.

resources.title: Kenyan traffic laws
resources.summary: The Traffic Act sets the rules of the road. Read the official text on Kenya Law and follow NTSA guidance.

steps: Always wear seat belts, carry your licence and obey speed limits and road signs.
Never drive under the influence of alcohol or drugs.
Motorcycle riders and passengers must wear helmets and reflective jackets.
Read the full Traffic Act and its rules on Kenya Law.

resources.source_name: Kenya Law (National Council for Law Reporting)

resources.title: Fuel prices (EPRA)
resources.summary: EPRA sets maximum pump prices on the 14th of every month for the period from the 15th to the 14th of the next month.

steps: See our fuel price tracker below for the current cycle in major towns.
Prices differ by town because of transport costs.
For any town, check EPRA's full price list.

resources.title: Road closures and traffic disruptions
resources.summary: KeNHA announces closures and diversions on national highways. Approved notices appear in our notices section.

steps: Check KeNHA's official notices before long journeys.
Follow diversion signs and police instructions on the road.
Allow extra time during announced works or events.

resources.title: Airports
resources.summary: Kenya Airports Authority runs the main airports, including JKIA (Nairobi), Moi International (Mombasa) and Kisumu International.

steps: Check flight status with your airline — schedules change.
Arrive early for security screening, especially for international flights.
See KAA's website for airport services and notices.

resources.title: Travel advisories
resources.summary: Before travelling abroad, check advice from Kenya's Ministry of Foreign and Diaspora Affairs and register with the Kenyan mission.

steps: Read current advisories on the Ministry of Foreign and Diaspora Affairs website.
Register with the nearest Kenyan embassy or consulate when you arrive abroad.
Within Kenya, check weather warnings from the Kenya Meteorological Department before road trips.

resources.source_name: Ministry of Foreign and Diaspora Affairs

resources.title: 2027 school calendar
resources.summary: Term dates for 2027 from the Ministry of Education circular dated 19 October 2026. See the interactive calendar below.

steps: Term One opens on Monday 4 January 2027 for all schools.
Pre-primary, primary and junior school: Term 1 to 9 April; Term 2 3 May–30 July; Term 3 30 August–5 November.
Senior/secondary school: Term 1 to 2 April; Term 2 3 May–30 July.
KNEC primary and junior assessments: 1–5 November 2027. KCSE: 8–26 November 2027.
content.caution: Reported from the Ministry's circular (ref. MOE.HQS/3/13/3 VOL III). The Ministry's website could not be reached when we checked, and some outlets printed conflicting dates — confirm with your school.

resources.source_name: Ministry of Education — State Department for Basic Education

resources.title: National exams and results (KNEC)
resources.summary: KNEC runs KPSEA (Grade 6), KJSEA (Grade 9) and KCSE. Results are released online.

steps: 2026 KJSEA results: the Education Cabinet Secretary said they are targeted for December 2026, ahead of Grade 10 placement.
2026 KCSE results: targeted for January 2027. No exact date had been announced when we checked.
Check results only through KNEC's official channels (knec.ac.ke).
Ignore anyone offering to 'upgrade' or release results early for money — it is a scam.

resources.title: Applying to university
resources.summary: Government-sponsored places at public universities and colleges are allocated by KUCCPS based on KCSE results and programme requirements.

steps: Check each programme's minimum KCSE mean grade and subject (cluster) requirements on the KUCCPS portal.
Apply or revise your choices during the KUCCPS application window.
Self-sponsored places are applied for directly with the university.
Only study at universities listed by the Commission for University Education.

resources.title: KUCCPS placement
resources.summary: KUCCPS places students in universities, colleges and TVET institutions. Applications and revisions are done online.

steps: Log in to the KUCCPS students portal with your KCSE index number and year.
Choose programmes in order of preference and pay the application fee shown.
Check placement results on the same portal.
Follow the institution's admission instructions to report.
content.processing: The 2026 placement window for KCSE 2025 candidates opened on 7 April 2026.

resources.title: HELB and university/TVET funding
resources.summary: Government funding for university and TVET students combines scholarships, loans and bursaries based on need, applied for through HELB and the Higher Education Financing portal.

steps: First-time students apply after placement through the official funding portal.
Continuing students apply for subsequent loans each year on HELB.
Keep your documents ready: ID, KCSE details, admission letter and household information.
Repay loans on time after graduation to avoid penalties.
content.processing: The 2026/27 first-time application window closed after an extension to 21 September 2026. Watch HELB for the next window.

resources.title: Government scholarships
resources.summary: The Ministry of Education publishes foreign government scholarships for which Kenya nominates candidates, and HEF awards need-based scholarships.

steps: Check the Ministry of Education's scholarships page regularly for nomination calls.
Some programmes (such as Hungary's Stipendium Hungaricum) require you to apply both to the host country and to the Ministry as the 'sending partner'.
Need-based scholarships for university and TVET students are applied for through the Higher Education Financing portal.
content.caution: The Ministry of Education's website (education.go.ke/scholarships) could not be reached when we checked; nomination calls are published there.

resources.source_name: Ministry of Education; Higher Education Financing

resources.title: International scholarships for Kenyans
resources.summary: A directory of major international scholarships open to Kenyans, with their current status. See the scholarship directory below.

steps: Read each programme's eligibility rules on its official website.
Prepare documents early — transcripts, references and essays take time.
Never pay anyone to 'guarantee' a scholarship.

resources.title: Accredited universities
resources.summary: Only study at universities approved by the Commission for University Education (CUE). Degrees from unapproved institutions are not recognised.

steps: Check the university on CUE's status of universities page before paying fees.
Check that the specific programme is accredited too.
CUE's March 2026 list had 36 public universities, 7 public constituent colleges, 32 chartered private universities and 2 private constituent colleges.

resources.title: TVET institutions
resources.summary: Technical and vocational colleges must be registered by TVETA. Government-sponsored TVET places are also offered through KUCCPS.

steps: Check that the college is registered and accredited by TVETA.
Apply through KUCCPS for government-sponsored places or directly to the college.
TVET students can apply for government funding through the financing portal.

resources.title: Competency-Based Education and senior school pathways
resources.summary: Under Competency-Based Education, the first learners joined Grade 10 (senior school) in January 2026 and chose one of three pathways.

steps: Pathways: STEM; Arts and Sports Science; Social Sciences.
Senior school runs from Grade 10 to Grade 12.
Grade 10 placement combines KPSEA (20%), school-based assessments in Grades 7–8 (20%) and KJSEA (60%), as reported by the Ministry.
KICD develops the curriculum designs and approved materials.

resources.title: Teacher recruitment (TSC)
resources.summary: Teacher jobs and internships are advertised only by the Teachers Service Commission on its official website.

steps: Apply only through the TSC online portal — manual applications are not accepted for national adverts.
TSC has repeatedly warned about fake recruitment adverts; check every advert on tsc.go.ke.
Make sure your TSC registration (certificate) is up to date.

emergency.name: Ambulance dispatch
emergency.description: National Ambulance Dispatch Centre (SHA). Free on all networks.

emergency.name: Child helpline
emergency.description: Report child abuse or get help for a child.

calendar.title: Term 1 opens (all schools)

scholarships.name: Chevening Scholarships
scholarships.eligibility: Citizens of Chevening-eligible countries, including Kenya. See the official eligibility page.
scholarships.notes: Applications for 2027–2028 are closed. The page lists the usual cycle as opening in August and closing in October; next dates not yet announced.

scholarships.name: Commonwealth Master's Scholarships
scholarships.institution: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK
scholarships.eligibility: Citizens of eligible Commonwealth countries (Kenya is eligible) who cannot afford UK study; 2:1 degree or equivalent; apply through a nominating agency.
scholarships.coverage: Airfare, full tuition, monthly stipend (£1,712; £2,000 in London), travel grant, some child allowances.

scholarships.name: Stipendium Hungaricum
scholarships.institution: Government of Hungary / Tempus Public Foundation
scholarships.eligibility: Applicants nominated by their country's sending partner; for Kenya, the Ministry of Education. Apply to both.
scholarships.coverage: Tuition-free study, monthly stipend and housing allowance (amounts on the official site).
scholarships.notes: The 2026 call closed on 15 January 2026. There is one deadline per year; the 2027/28 call date was not published on the official page when checked.

scholarships.name: Türkiye Scholarships (Türkiye Bursları)
scholarships.eligibility: International applicants; merit-based. Check nationality and age rules on the official site.
scholarships.coverage: Financial support and university placement — details on the official site.
scholarships.notes: Official calendar lists the general application period as 10 January – 20 February each year.

scholarships.name: DAAD Scholarships
scholarships.eligibility: Depends on each programme; some are specifically for developing countries (e.g. EPOS).
scholarships.coverage: Monthly payment (e.g. €992 for students, €1,300 for doctoral candidates), travel allowance, often insurance.
scholarships.notes: Deadlines differ by programme — search the DAAD scholarship database.

scholarships.name: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program
scholarships.eligibility: Talented young people with financial need, through partner institutions. PhD candidates are not currently eligible.
scholarships.coverage: Tuition, accommodation, books, mentoring, leadership development and, if needed, a return air ticket.
scholarships.notes: Each partner university sets its own deadline.
